primary_claim: Fine-tuning the scalar prefactor of a single German-specific parameter subcomponent (from adversarial parameter decomposition) destroys a 67M-parameter model's German-language ability (CE driven to the ~10.83-nat chance level) using as few as ~4 German training tokens with <0.1 nats English CE increase, beating rank-1/rank-4 LoRA (which need ~32 tokens) and, unlike the LoRA baselines, leaves French and Spanish performance almost untouched without explicit regularization for those languages.

effect.metric: German training tokens needed to drive German CE to chance (~10.83 nats) with <0.1 nats English CE increase

stated_future_work: extend this to allow learning new circuits by letting the fine-tune change parameter subcomponents along select directions corresponding to specific other subcomponents' U and V vectors (a 'blueprint' approach)
do proper follow-up work to confirm the Lp-penalty approach (changing masks without specifying which subcomponents) holds up
limitations_stated: this is a single fine-tuning target for a single decomposition of a single 67M Pile model
the model doesn't know that much German to begin with; it's the model's best non-English language but still far weaker than English
if there are plenty of German tokens to train on, and regularisation covers everything we want to protect, the LoRAs are probably still better
performance on Italian was heavily damaged
quote: We can destroy a 67M-parameter language model's ability to predict German text by fine-tuning a single number: the scalar prefactor on one German-related rank-1 parameter subcomponent.
